summary: Morgan County's first fire tower, an 80-foot steel Aermotor on Union Hill, went up in 1964 and was sold to a private owner in 2019; access is by permission.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 steel tower with 7 by 7 foot cab

access.note: Access is now only by permission of the landowner, according to the register.

facts.agency: Private owner since 2019; earlier Alabama Forestry Commission

events.note: Erected in 1964; 1964 press calls it Morgan County's first and only fire tower
Tower and site sold or deeded to a private owner; access now by permission

evidence.quote: Union Hill Lookout Tower was erected in 1964

evidence.supports: high hill in eastern Morgan County
evidence.quote: Located on a high hill in the eastern part of the county

evidence.supports: county's first and only fire tower, made of steel
evidence.quote: Morgan County's first, and only, fire tower is made of steel.
It is an Aermotor MC-39 steel tower with 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: one of a limited number of 80-foot towers in Alabama
evidence.quote: one of a limited number of 80' towers used in Alabama
The tower itself is 80 feet in height
Morgan County's first fire tower is nearing completion.

evidence.supports: April 1964 in operation, not quite finished
evidence.quote: not quite completed yet, is nevertheless in operation

evidence.supports: July 1964 not yet manned, lack of funds and personnel
evidence.quote: Due to the lack of funds and personnel, the newly erected fire tower in the eastern part of Morgan County has not yet been manned.

evidence.supports: sold to a private owner in 2019
evidence.quote: The tower and surrounding buildings were sold to a private owner in 2019.

evidence.supports: access now only by permission of the landowner
evidence.quote: Access is now only by permission of the landowner.

evidence.supports: site deeded to private ownership, August 2019
evidence.quote: August 2019: The lookout site deeded to private ownership.

evidence.supports: Alabama Forestry Commission as earlier administrator

corrections.why: The tower and site were sold or deeded to a private owner in 2019, so the record's state ownership is out of date.

notes_for_editor: The Decatur Daily wording is as reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the newspaper originals were not read. The 2019 sale rests on the NHLR and Forest Lookouts pages; one WebSearch found no independent confirmation. Staffing after 1964 and any fire history are unknown. The register's elevation (1,274 ft) is not used.
